title: Zero Distance
description: A customer accidentally sets the same address as both origin and destination. The pricing formula should still hold together at the degenerate zero-distance boundary rather than erroring or producing a nonsensical negative fee.
successCondition: POST /api/booking/quote with origin and destination set to identical lat/lng coordinates returns 200 with distanceKm equal to 0 (or a value effectively 0, within floating point noise), distanceFeeCents equal to 0, and priceCents equal to exactly baseFeeCents + weightFeeCents.
hints: The haversine formula naturally returns ~0 for identical points, but floating-point sin/cos math can leave a tiny nonzero residue — assert with a small tolerance rather than exact equality on distanceKm.
distanceFeeCents is round(distanceKm * 8), so even a tiny residual distanceKm should still round to exactly 0 cents.
